descriptions.title: Why a registry, not a framework
descriptions.body: CypherMiner deliberately ships no UI framework. Every tool is a self-contained object matching the Tool interface in src/types.ts; importing the module calls register() (core/registry.ts) and pushes it into an in-memory list. The UI shell (core/ui.ts) reads that list to auto-build the sidebar, search, the input form (from tool.inputs), the live result panel, the copy button and any optional visual. The payoff: adding a tool is dropping one file into src/tools/<category>/ and adding one import line in src/tools/index.ts — no routing, no form code, no wiring. The catalog and the interface can never drift apart because the interface IS the catalog.

descriptions.title: Local-first and genuinely offline
descriptions.body: Every tool runs in the browser with zero network calls. Ciphers, encoders, hashing (Web Crypto), number theory (BigInt) and text utilities are all pure client-side functions. vite-plugin-pwa registers a service worker so the static build is installable and keeps working with no connection. The only Python in the picture is an optional FastAPI backend reserved for future heavy/data tools — the 59 shipping tools need no server at all. This is a privacy guarantee, not just a feature: sensitive text never leaves the device.

descriptions.title: Bilingual to the core (Loc pairs)
descriptions.body: Bilingual EN/PT support is structural, not bolted on. The type system defines Lang = 'en' | 'pt' and Loc = Record<Lang, string>, and every user-facing string in the codebase is a Loc pair: UI labels (i18n.ts), tool names and blurbs, input labels, select options, and the entire educational layer (history, trivia, sources in src/content/). loc() resolves the active language with an English fallback; setLang() persists the choice and re-renders instantly. The on-device assistant indexes both languages at once.

descriptions.title: The on-device assistant (TF-IDF retrieval)
descriptions.body: assistant/local.ts builds a weighted token index over each tool's bilingual name, blurb, category and educational content, with stop-words for both languages, a synonym map (e.g. 'password' -> hash/sha/md5), accent normalisation and light de-pluralisation. It scores tools with squared-IDF weighting so rare, specific terms (like 'palindrome') outrank generic ones (like 'cipher'), boosts the tool you're currently viewing, and answers context-aware questions ('how does this work?'). It returns up to three matches above a 40% relevance cutoff — all computed in the browser. A cloud provider (assistant/cloud.ts) can take over by config when the suite is published.

descriptions.title: Visuals generated from inputs
descriptions.body: Several crypto tools render a live diagram as you type. caesar.ts builds an SVG cipher wheel from the current shift; widgets/visuals.ts provides reusable builders — a two-row mapping strip with active-letter highlighting (substitution-style ciphers), a 5x5 Polybius grid with row/column headers, and a rail-fence zigzag grid. The UI runner calls tool.visual(values, container, ctx) on every input change, so the picture always matches the output.

descriptions.title: Heavy math done right (BigInt)
descriptions.body: The mathematics category does real number theory rather than float approximations. factor.ts implements Miller-Rabin primality testing over a fixed witness set, Pollard's rho with Brent-style cycle detection, and recursive factorization — all in BigInt — so it can factor large integers and group results as p^e. Lottery odds and combinatorics use exact BigInt combination counts (nCrBig) so the probabilities are precise, not rounded.

descriptions.title: Runtime config without a rebuild
descriptions.body: core/config.ts fetches ./config.json (cache:'no-store') at startup and merges it over typed defaults (assistantMode, cloudEndpoint, lotteryWizUrl, showAllTools). On a published site an operator can edit config.json to switch the assistant to cloud mode, point lottery tools at a deployed LotteryWiz, or expand the default sidebar — all without rebuilding. If the file is missing (e.g. first offline load) the defaults apply silently.
